Eve —

Quick scan from capacity side (numbers rounded / live inventory as of 2026-10-29 10:00 PT):
- Total H100 GPUs across us-west clusters: 28 H100 (12 in Dedicated pools, 16 in shared pool)
- Total A100 GPUs across us-west clusters: 112 A100 (mixed gen)
- Equivalent conversion: 1 H100 ~= 3.5 A100 for our workload profiles (batch vs streaming differs).

Customer target: 40 H100-equivalent concurrent => roughly 140 A100-equivalent if using raw conversion, but because inference footprint will be quantized and they plan 8k token windows typical, a mixed approach works: 16 H100 + 48 A100 (as hot nodes) gives similar throughput with fallback to A100-only mode.

Options:
1) Short soft-hold (14 days): we can earmark up to 16 H100-equivalent capacity (either H100 or A100 pool reallocation) without requiring contractual reserved capacity. This requires ops approval and a change freeze window allocation.
2) Medium hold (2-6 weeks): requires a monetary credit (reservation commitment) and coordination with capacity planner — we can set a standby pool of ~24 A100 + 8 H100 for testing + canary.
3) Long hold (>6 weeks / convert to Dedicated): needs formal Dedicated capacity commit and finance approval. Lead time ~4–6 weeks to formalize.

Immediate recommendation: approve a 14-day soft-hold starting 2026-11-10 for a canary of 4 H100-equivalent (for their integration tests) and earmark an additional soft buffer of A100s (24 A100s) that we can convert to Dedicated if they sign. That buys sales time and keeps runway.

Notes:
- We have a major internal push week of cluster maintenance scheduled 2026-11-18—22; if we approve a soft-hold that spans that week, we'll need to ensure the hold is respected during the maintenance window.
- Ops prefers concrete dates; give us target start and an SLA expectation from Sales (is 99th percentile latency important for them or is throughput more important?).

I'll attach a quick inventory snapshot (equinox_capacity_scan.xlsx updated) and a node-mix sketch (equinox_map.xlsx).

—Logan

Thanks Logan — good write-up. Operational constraints to call out for Sales/Legal:

- Soft-hold policy: our baseline policy allows up to 14 calendar days of capacity earmark with no financial commitment. Anything beyond 14 days requires either (a) a reservation credit in HubSpot/Finance or (b) an MSA addendum signed that authorizes the hold.
- Approval chain: Capacity Lead (Logan) -> Head of Serving Ops -> Finance (for credit) -> Legal (for MSA addendum). We can fast-track if Sales confirms intent to sign within the hold window.
- Canary allocation: can provision a 4 H100-equivalent canary (or 12 A100s) within 48 hours of approval if the cluster maintenance window isn't blocking it. Note the maintenance window 11/18–11/22 may require scheduling the canary earlier.

Operational ask for Sales (to confirm):
1) Desired soft-hold start date (exact day).
2) Expected conversion timing (if they plan to sign within X days).
3) Canary size and test schedule (integration smoke/throughput targets).

If Sales can confirm a start date of 2026-11-10 and that they intend to execute PO within 14 days, we can approve the soft-hold now and queue the canary. Otherwise we propose the 14-day window and then a short-term paid standby for weeks 3–12.
